ConocoPhillips fell 0.83% today as oil prices retreated across the board—US crude dropped to $83.90 per barrel, down from higher levels earlier in the week. This decline came amid diplomatic developments in the Middle East, where Qatar's prime minister visited Iran for de-escalation talks and Iran announced a revenue-sharing deal with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz. These moves suggest reduced immediate tension in one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints, easing near-term concerns about supply disruptions that had supported prices earlier.

The broader pullback also reflects investor reassessment after earlier fears around tanker attacks and geopolitical risk proved less severe than initially priced in. At the same time, Europe's historically low gas storage heading into winter could support longer-term energy demand, though that hasn't offset today's focus on the diplomatic shift reducing short-term supply anxiety.
